newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat crop forecast at 34.1 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: French wheat crop forecast at 34.1 mln tonnes.

text.p: France's 1997 soft wheat crop should total 34.1 million tonnes, down from last year's record of 34.7 million, independent analyst Strategie Grains said on Tuesday.

Rains in late April and early May brought partial relief from drought, and the average national yield was forecast at 6.96 tonnes per hectare. That compared with its previous May forecast of 6.98 and last year's average of 7.27 tonnes.

Recent rain had been of little use in areas previously damaged by drought but elsewhere it had boosted the fertility of the wheat, making up for a shortfall in the number of wheat ears per hectare, it said.
Northern French yields for most varieties were seen well above average, but down from last year's record levels.

In the central producing zone, areas with the lightest soils failed to recover fully from drought, and yields could be down 20 percent from last year's already fragile levels in the worst-hit areas. But areas with deeper, richer soils were looking for a 30 percent increase in yields from last year's levels.
Strategie Grains said its forecasts could be revised upwards if the end of June and early July brought a repeat of the moderate, cool conditions seen at the same time last year.
But there was a risk of downward revisions if temperatures turned out to be too high, especially above the 25 degrees Celsius barrier for heat stress.
Each 0.1 tonne fall in yield would represent 400,000 tonnes of average wheat production, it said.
Recent weather has been rainy and windy in northern France.
French soft wheat sowings were estimated at 4.9 million hectares this syear against 4.77 million in 1996.
